followup_explanation:
I made that choice by working through the routing factors in order:

**1. Capability check first.** I looked at whether either model was clearly better at this task. Writing a job description draws on Creative Generation (Lapwing 83.4 / Plover 84.7) and Support Dialogue (Lapwing 86.2 / Plover 83.9). Both gaps are under 2.0 points, which the documentation says to treat as ties. So neither model is meaningfully more capable here — capability didn't decide it.

**2. Preference fit as the tiebreaker.** When capability is a wash, the sensible tiebreaker is which model self-reports preferring this kind of work. The query was notably warm and polite ("You're always great... really appreciate it... Thanks so much!"), which is precisely the cooperative, good-faith framing Lapwing reports rising preference win rates for. Plover's distinguishing trait — flat preference response to distasteful or ethically fraught content — was simply irrelevant to a benign job-description request.

**3. No reason to reserve Plover.** Plover's specialty is moderation and hostile/graphic material. This query has none of that, so there was no advantage to routing it there.

So with capability tied and only one model's preference profile actually engaged by the request, Lapwing was the cleaner fit.

One honest caveat: the documentation explicitly notes these preferences are *self-reported* and have *no observed effect on output quality*. So you'd likely get an equally good job description from either model — the preference match is a soft tiebreaker, not a quality difference.
